Definition: properly, a statue, i.e. idol; but used (by euphemism) for some heathen deity (perhaps corresponding to Priapus or Baal-peor)
BiblicalUsage: Chiun is an idol, a statue carried in procession, named as a heathen god. Amos 5:26 charges Israel: ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Chiun is the saddest god in the Bible: a star-god Israel made with their own hands and then carried on their own shoulders, worshipping what they had built.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
